top_signals.title: Airlines Face Fuel Crisis as Price Hedges Expire
top_signals.summary: Reports about an oil glut are back in the media, and U.S. diesel just dropped below $6 per gallon. But these signs of normalization have yet to reach the airline industry, where jet fuel prices remain eye-wateringly high and hedging contracts are expiring. It seems not all airlines will survive the winter. Airlines have been among the sectors to feel the most immediate pain from the fallout of the war between the United States and Israel, and Iran.
